records.name: Anderson Monarchs
records.summary: A youth sports nonprofit that teaches baseball and other sports to kids in Philadelphia from a young age through high school, with a focus on young people who have fewer resources.
records.what_you_do: Kids play several sports year round and also work on school and leadership goals. The site does not describe volunteer coach or mentor roles.

cost.text: Not stated on the site. The site asks for donations, but no program fees are listed.

first_step.how: Email info@andersonmonarchs.org. The site does not say how a child or volunteer joins.
first_step.basis: The only contact on the site is an email address, and the sign-up steps are not described.

records.notes: Status is dormant because the newest dated item on the site is from November 2022, even though the home page is live. The directory lists soccer and basketball too; the dated pages only name baseball, so only baseball is tagged. Ages and cost are not stated. Verify before showing a sign-up path.

records.name: Change Up Sports
records.summary: A free softball and baseball group that runs clinics, camps, leagues, and training for young people and adults in Philadelphia. It also runs programs in Sierra Leone and Belize.
records.what_you_do: Players can join free youth and adult clinics, camps, and leagues. Supporters can donate equipment, host a drive, or join a service trip abroad. The site does not list local coach roles.

cost.text: Free. The group says it never charges participants for its programs.

first_step.how: Use the Get Involved page to donate or join a volunteer trip. The page does not explain how to register for a local clinic.
first_step.basis: Programs are free, but the page does not say how to register for a local clinic.

records.notes: The directory lists a changeupsports.org address that does not resolve; the working site is letschangeupsports.org. The site has no dated items, so status is probably_active. Volunteer trip dates are to be posted later. A directory entry for Philadelphia Adult League Softball (phillypals.com) is listed under the Change Up Sports name, but it is an adult league, so it is not recorded here.

records.name: Skate The Foundry
records.summary: A skate school in West Philadelphia that teaches skateboarding and roller skating to kids, teens, and adults, with after-school, weekend, and camp options and open skate time.
records.what_you_do: Kids can join a Thursday after-school skateboard club, a youth weekend program, or camps on school days off. Open skate and open training sessions are listed. The site does not list volunteer roles.

schedule.text: Thursday after-school skateboard club, youth weekend programs, camps on school days off, and open skate sessions. Exact times are on the site.

cost.text: Lessons and membership cost money. Prices are not on the home page. New students get 15 percent off a first private lesson.

first_step.how: Book a class, camp, or open skate online, or call 215-954-0750.
first_step.basis: Beginner riders are welcome, and the site lists a new-student discount and open skate sessions.

records.notes: No skateboarding tag exists in the vocabulary, so youth_coaching is the closest fit. The site lists Spring Round 2 start dates (April 18, 19, and 23) without a year, so status is probably_active rather than active. Membership and lesson prices are not on the home page.

records.name: B Inspired Philadelphia
records.summary: A nonprofit that runs after-school programs for kindergarten through 8th grade students in under-resourced parts of Philadelphia, with art, fitness, money skills, and wellness classes run with partner groups.
records.what_you_do: Students join partner-run after-school classes, such as an art program for grades 3 to 8. The site does not describe volunteer roles or how to sign up.

locations.label: Partner program sites, including Morton McMichael School and The Barnes Foundation

cost.text: Not stated on the pages read.

first_step.how: Not stated on the pages read. Programs run through partner schools and groups.
first_step.basis: Students join through partner programs, and the sign-up steps are not on the site.

records.notes: The newest dated item on the site is from 2021 (after-school art programs starting for grades 3 to 8). Only the year is known, so no month is written and last_sign_of_life is left out. The directory lists this group under General Athletics, but the site shows no sports teams, so it is filed under after-school and arts programs.

records.name: Beat the Streets Philadelphia
records.summary: A sports and learning group that uses wrestling, mentoring, and tutoring to help student athletes in under-served parts of Philadelphia do well in school.
records.what_you_do: Students can join a wrestling team or use the Mentoring Center for school help. The group is recruiting coaches, and mentors are often college student athletes from Drexel and Penn.

cost.text: Not stated on the pages read.

first_step.how: Coaches: use the resources page to apply. Mentors: use the mentoring page. Parents and students seeking academic help: contact the Mentoring Coordinator to set a first visit. Wrestlers: find a team near you on the site.
first_step.basis: Each role has a stated way in, and a first visit to the Mentoring Center is offered.

records.notes: Ages are not stated, so crowd is only students. Wrestling has no tag in the vocabulary, so youth_coaching is used. The February 19, 2026 benefit is the dated evidence. Roles are written as help_teach for both coaches and mentors.

records.name: Harlem Lacrosse Philadelphia
records.summary: A lacrosse program that uses the sport to support middle and high school students in the Olney area, with more than 200 students served.
records.what_you_do: Students play lacrosse through school-based programs at Thomas K. Finletter School, Olney High School, and Olney Elementary School. A Volunteer button on the site leads to a sign-up page.

locations.label: Program sites: Thomas K. Finletter School, Olney High School, and Olney Elementary School

cost.text: Fees are not stated. The site has a scholarships link, but its details were not on the page read.

first_step.how: Use the Volunteer page for volunteering. The site does not explain how a student joins.
first_step.basis: The program runs through schools, and the sign-up steps for students are not on the page.

records.notes: The page lists August and September 2026 coverage, and a current regional newsletter. Dated items were read from the page text, not from the article links, which were not captured. Harlem Lacrosse is a wider organization; this record covers the Philadelphia program only. Age range for the Olney Elementary site is not stated.

records.name: Work to Ride
records.summary: A free horse program at Chamounix Stables in Fairmount Park that gives under-resourced Philadelphia youth riding, horse care, and equine sports.
records.what_you_do: Youth can join Sunday sessions at the stables, riding lessons, or a summer camp for ages 7 to 13. Volunteers 14 and up start with barn chores and can move on to helping instructors teach lessons.

schedule.text: Sunday sessions at the stables (a newer program, start date not stated), riding lessons, and a summer camp in nine one-week sessions.

cost.text: The site says its riding experiences are free. Summer camp is funded by donations, and the page does not list fees.

first_step.how: Volunteers 14 and up can use the volunteer form linked from the site. Youth can check the site for how to join.
first_step.basis: Volunteers have a linked sign-up form, and the youth programs are described as free, but the page does not spell out how a youth signs up.

records.notes: The site was last updated October 6, 2026. The page menu held several unrelated pharmacy links; the fetch summary itself warned that the page may have been altered. Those links were ignored, and the volunteer form link is not copied here, so check it on the official page before use. Summer camp ages (7 to 13) come from the site text. The flagship program's age range is not stated. Volunteers 14 and up are the only age floor on the page.

records.name: Street Soccer USA Philadelphia
records.summary: A street soccer program with teams in four Philadelphia neighborhoods: North, West, Southwest Philadelphia, and Kensington.
records.what_you_do: Players can join a team at one of the four locations. Coaches and volunteers can apply through a form on the page.

locations.label: Four sites: North Philadelphia, West Philadelphia, Southwest Philadelphia, and Kensington

cost.text: Not stated on the page read.

first_step.how: To join a team, email taz@streetsoccerusa.org. Coaches and volunteers can use the apply form on the page.
first_step.basis: The page names a contact to join a team and a form for coaches and volunteers.

records.notes: The page has no dates, so status is probably_active. Ages are not stated, so no age range is given. Street Soccer USA is a national organization; this record covers the Philadelphia page only.

records.name: Arlen Specter US Squash Center
records.summary: A squash center that runs junior programs, a summer squash camp for players of every skill level, lessons, and club events.
records.what_you_do: Kids and teens can join junior programs, lessons, and the summer squash camp. The site also lists memberships and venue rentals. Volunteer coach or mentor roles are not listed.

cost.text: Memberships, lessons, and camps are offered, but prices are not on the home page.

first_step.how: Use the Membership or Squash Lessons links on the site. The site welcomes players of any experience level.
first_step.basis: The site says it welcomes players and families regardless of experience, and it lists a camp for every skill level.

records.notes: The street address was not read, so no location is listed; confirm before adding one. The site lists a June 2026 youth sports award and a September 2026 post. The site lists no volunteer coach or mentor roles.

records.name: Playworks Philadelphia
records.summary: A nonprofit that helps kids stay active through games at school recess and in youth programs, with a Philadelphia office on East High Street.
records.what_you_do: Individual volunteers are trained and supported to be a steady, caring adult at partner schools, and they can teach sports basics. Individuals apply through an open opportunities link, and companies can request a group volunteer day.

cost.text: Not stated on the pages read.

first_step.how: Individuals apply through the open opportunities link on the volunteer page.
first_step.basis: Volunteers have a clear apply link, and training is provided.

records.notes: The volunteer page covers Pennsylvania statewide and does not name Philadelphia schools, so no partner school is listed. Ages are not given; the site refers to kids and children. The August 2026 item is a news post about the state recess rule.

records.name: Girls on the Run Philadelphia
records.summary: A seasonal running program for girls in 3rd to 8th grade that builds social, emotional, and physical skills through running and group talks, led by trained volunteer coaches.
records.what_you_do: Girls join a 3rd to 5th grade team or a 6th to 8th grade team for a season. Volunteers can coach, help at the 5K, or sign up through the volunteer page.

cost.text: The registration fee is not on the home page. The group says donations help make sure no girl is turned away for money reasons.

first_step.how: Use the coach and volunteer pages linked from the site.
first_step.basis: Separate coach and volunteer pages are linked, but the sign-up steps are not on the home page.

records.notes: The home page has no dated news, and the 5K date (December 6) has no year, so status is probably_active. The page's copyright year is not used as evidence. Ages are a grade range, not years.

records.name: Students Run Philly Style
records.summary: A free running program for Philadelphia students in grades 6 to 12 that trains them toward a half or full marathon, with volunteer mentors called Running Leaders.
records.what_you_do: Students train with a team and a mentor up to 10 hours a week from March to November. Running Leaders co-lead practices, usually after school or on Saturday mornings.

schedule.text: Training runs March through November for the November Philadelphia Half or Full Marathon. Running Leaders co-lead 2 to 3 practices a week, usually 3 to 5 pm or Saturday mornings.

cost.text: Free for participants. The site says race entries, transportation, and running gear are included.

first_step.how: Mentors: fill in the interest form on the volunteer mentor page. Enrollment reopens in August 2026. Students: check the site for enrollment.
first_step.basis: Mentors need an interest form, mandatory training, a background check, and to be 21 or older. Student sign-up steps were not read.

records.notes: The press dates come from the article addresses (October 13, 2025 and November 21, 2025). The mentor page says enrollment reopens in August 2026. Mentor requirements per the site: age 21 or older, mandatory Running Leader training, an online course, and Pennsylvania state background checks, which the group can help with. Mentor cost is not stated. The site lists 400 mentors in its impact figures.

records.name: Mentor Leaders Produce Mentor Leaders
records.summary: A mentoring nonprofit that works with young people ages 10 to 24 through one-on-one and group mentoring, life skills training, and job pathways for top mentees.
records.what_you_do: Young people can join as mentees through a form on the site, or book a call. The site describes mentor roles only in general terms, so volunteer mentoring is not recorded.

cost.text: Fees are not stated. The site lists financial incentives for mentees based on achievement.

first_step.how: Join as a mentee using the form on the site, or use the Book A Call link.
first_step.basis: Entry is through a form and a call, and the site does not describe the steps after that.

records.notes: Dated items are from 2025 only (a community award and an annual report, without months), so status is probably_active. The page tagline references Philadelphia; the city address was not read. Volunteer mentor roles and requirements are not described, so none are recorded.

records.name: Special Olympics Pennsylvania
records.summary: The Pennsylvania chapter of Special Olympics, with a Greater Philadelphia region, offering free sports training and competitions for athletes of all ages, including a Young Athletes program for ages 2 to 7.
records.what_you_do: Athletes train and compete in many sports at no cost. Volunteers, including coaches, sign up through the volunteer portal and can join a monthly info call.

cost.text: Athletes pay nothing, according to the site.

first_step.how: Sign up as an athlete or volunteer through the volunteer page or portal, or join a monthly info call.
first_step.basis: The site lists a program for ages 2 to 7, monthly info calls, and a volunteer portal.

records.notes: The site is statewide. Its Greater Philadelphia staff are listed on the Meet Our Team page, which was not read. The home page lists an October 6, 2026 post. The fall festival is at Villanova in November 2026, outside the city. Coach needs in Philadelphia specifically are not stated.

records.name: Independence Youth Cycling
records.summary: A youth cycling group that runs mountain biking, cyclocross, bike clinics, and team riding for young riders, with several teams that carry the Philly name.
records.what_you_do: Young riders join a team or a clinic. The site lists coaching and volunteerism as a program area but does not describe how to volunteer.

cost.text: Fees are not stated. The site links a team FAQ that may cover costs, but it was not read.

first_step.how: The site links a team director and head coach portal. Team sign-up is through the site.
first_step.basis: Teams are joined through a portal, and the page does not explain the steps.

records.notes: The newest dated item is a June 2024 registration post linked from the home page, so status is dormant. Its article address was not captured. The site also lists 2023 sponsor thanks. Ages are not stated.

records.name: Philadelphia Youth Basketball
records.summary: A basketball group for young people from kindergarten through high school in Philadelphia, with programs that include mentorship, summer offerings, and holiday clinics.
records.what_you_do: Kids join basketball programs, clinics, and summer offerings, and older teens can get mentorship and internship chances. The group has a volunteer page.

cost.text: Fees are not stated on the home page. The group links a scholarships page.

first_step.how: Use the volunteer link to offer help. Program pages list the enrollment steps.
first_step.basis: Program listings and a volunteer link are on the home page, but the sign-up steps were not read.

records.notes: The home page lists September 2026 press coverage of a planned workforce building set to open in 2029, which is the dated evidence. The group says it has 350 or more volunteers and staff. Whether it needs new volunteer coaches is not stated.

records.name: Team Up Philly
records.summary: A free program for girls in under-served Philadelphia communities that offers sports and enrichment, including tutoring and academic help.
records.what_you_do: Girls can join free sports and enrichment programs, including tutoring. Volunteers can use the volunteer link, and the group also runs summer scholarships and events.

cost.text: Programs are described as free on the site.

first_step.how: Contact the group through its website. The sign-up steps were not on the page read.
first_step.basis: Programs are free, but the page does not explain how a girl or a volunteer signs up.

records.notes: The site shows an October 2026 blog post and a June 2026 benefit. Its program list names tutoring; sports content is not spelled out. Volunteer coach or mentor needs are not stated.

records.name: Neighborhood Bike Works
records.summary: A community bike shop that teaches young people to fix bikes and gives youth a chance to earn a bike, with weekday after-school hours and a Saturday open shop.
records.what_you_do: Youth join weekday programs to learn bike repair. Graduates of the programs can use the Saturday open shop to work on bikes.

schedule.text: Youth programs run Monday to Thursday, 4 to 6 pm (summer hours may vary). A Saturday youth open shop runs 10 am to 2 pm.

cost.text: Fees are not stated. The site says youth can earn a bike, but it does not explain how.

first_step.how: Fill in the Youth Programs Interest Form on the site.
first_step.basis: Youth join through an interest form, and the Saturday open shop is for graduates of the programs.

records.notes: No dated items are on the site, so status is probably_active. Adult programs are for ages 18 and up. Volunteer or mentor roles are not on the page. The youth age range is not stated.

records.name: Parks and Rec Youth Soccer League
records.summary: The city's Parks and Recreation youth soccer league for kids ages 7 to 14, with no experience needed. Indoor play runs January through April, and outdoor play runs September through November.
records.what_you_do: Teams play at local clubs, youth groups, and recreation centers. League directors help run the program, and a list of directors is posted.

schedule.text: Indoor league January through April. Outdoor league September through November.

cost.text: The city calls the league low-cost. The page does not list a fee per child or per team.

first_step.how: Contact your neighborhood recreation center, or call the Parks and Recreation main line at (215) 683-3600. Many activities need a Youth Participant Registration form.
first_step.basis: The league says no experience is needed, and the city publishes the season documents and a main phone line.

records.notes: The league page does not list coach or volunteer requirements. A search summary of city league documents mentioned background clearances for coaches and a per-team fee, but the 2025 indoor bylaws PDF did not extract as readable text, so those rules and fee amounts are left out and need checking. Indoor court locations are in a separate 2026 document, which was not read.

records.name: Parks and Rec Youth Baseball League
records.summary: The city's Parks and Recreation youth baseball league for Philadelphia kids ages 7 to 17, with no experience needed, playing outdoors from April through June.
records.what_you_do: Teams play at local clubs, youth groups, and recreation centers. Each season ends with playoffs, championships, and an awards banquet.

schedule.text: Outdoor season April through June, with playoffs and an awards banquet at the end.

cost.text: The city calls the league low-cost. The page does not list a fee per child or per team.

first_step.how: Return the youth registration form to the recreation center where the child will play, or call (215) 683-3600 with questions.
first_step.basis: The league says no experience is needed, and the city lists how to enroll.

records.notes: League documents are dated March 19, 2026. The page does not state coach or volunteer requirements. A bat specification document is dated December 2024. Confirm enrollment details with the department before sending anyone.

records.name: Philly Girls Baseball
records.summary: A nonprofit all-girls baseball program in Philadelphia for players ages 8 to 18, with teams, tournaments, and a need for volunteer coaches.
records.what_you_do: Girls join teams and play in outdoor-season tournaments, March through October. The group is adding volunteer coaches and asks applicants to email the program.

schedule.text: Outdoor season March through October, with tournaments through the fall. The 2026 DMV Series is October 10 to 11, 2026, in Maryland.

cost.text: 2026 packages were $180 per player (instructional) and $600 per player (all-inclusive), plus tournament fees. Scholarships are available by request.

first_step.how: Coaches: email info@phillygirlsbaseball.com with the subject Coaching at PGB. Families seeking help with cost can use the scholarship contact form.
first_step.basis: Coach applications and scholarship requests each have a clear contact route, though 2026 all-inclusive registration closed May 31.

records.notes: The home page lists two tournaments marked as completed in June and July 2026 and one upcoming tournament in October 2026. Coach requirements are background checks, abuse awareness training, and pitch smart training. The page does not mention mentors.

records.name: Torresdale Boys Club
records.summary: A Northeast Philadelphia club with baseball, softball, soccer, and basketball teams for boys and girls, with in-house and travel teams sorted by age.
records.what_you_do: Kids join in-house or travel teams by age and can take part in neighborhood social and community service events. Current updates are sent to a Facebook group.

cost.text: Fees and scholarships are not stated on the site.

first_step.how: The site sends families to its Facebook group for current information.
first_step.basis: The site gives no sign-up steps and points to a Facebook group.

records.notes: The site has no dated items, so status is probably_active. Ages, volunteer roles, and costs are not stated. The Facebook group is a lead only and was not read.

records.name: Philadelphia Youth Football Academy
records.summary: A sports-based youth development group for Philadelphia youth from low-income families, with flag football, a girls program, a summer camp, and a community league.
records.what_you_do: Youth can join flag football, the girls program, the summer camp, or the community league. The stated goals include healthy living, graduation, and job and college readiness.

cost.text: Fees, scholarships, and free programs are not stated on the site.

first_step.how: Use the Programs page for current options. The Programs page content was not captured, so sign-up steps are not recorded.
first_step.basis: The site lists program names, but the sign-up steps were not read.

records.notes: The site has no dated items, so status is probably_active. Ages are not stated. The site has no volunteer sign-up, so no volunteer roles are recorded.

records.name: PA Center for Adapted Sports
records.summary: An adapted sports center based at Boathouse Row that runs year-round programs in rowing, swimming, skiing, and track and field for children and adults.
records.what_you_do: Participants can join rowing, swimming, skiing, and track and field, including youth programs. The center has volunteer pages for general help and for adaptive rowing.

cost.text: Fees are not stated. The site says equipment, venues, and instruction are provided, with no fee listed.

first_step.how: Use the volunteer pages for volunteering, or the program pages for youth options.
first_step.basis: Several program and volunteer pages are linked, but sign-up steps are not on the home page.

records.notes: The site has no dated items, so status is probably_active. The center says it runs 13 programs year-round. The eligibility document it links was not read, so age limits are not recorded.

records.name: Girls in Gear
records.summary: A cycling program for girls of all ages and abilities, with coaches who run group sessions to build confidence.
records.what_you_do: Girls can join a session or find a ride near them. Coaches receive training in safety and the group's curriculum, and volunteers can use the coach link on the site.

cost.text: Fees, scholarships, and whether programs are free are not stated on the home page. A registration page is linked.

first_step.how: Register through the register page, or sign up as a coach through the coach page.
first_step.basis: Both a registration page and a coach page are linked from the home page.

records.notes: The site has no dated news, so status is probably_active. The Philadelphia link goes to a Greater Philadelphia page that was not read. Coach training is described, but no background check or minimum age is listed.

records.name: Kensington Soccer Club
records.summary: A soccer club founded in 2010 in Kensington, which says its programs are offered regardless of ability to pay.
records.what_you_do: The club links a program directory and a volunteer page from its home page, along with a calendar and news archive.

locations.label: Club office, 3400 J St., Room G4

cost.text: The club says its programs are offered regardless of ability to pay. Fees are not listed.

first_step.how: Use the program directory or the volunteer page linked from the home page.
first_step.basis: Links to programs and volunteering are present, but the sign-up steps are not on the home page.

records.notes: The site has no dated items with a year or month, so status is probably_active. Ages and youth program details are not stated on the home page, so the directory's soccer label is only partly confirmed.

records.name: Philly Youth Inc.
records.summary: A youth development group that runs a book club, self-care Saturdays, a young influencer feature, and global travel for teens.
records.what_you_do: Young people can join the book club, the self-care sessions, the Top Influencers feature for ages 12 to 25, or the global tours for teens. The site has a Volunteer With Us section.

cost.text: No program fees are listed. Donations cover travel and scholarships for teens who could not otherwise take part.

first_step.how: Use the Volunteer With Us section or the support page. Ages 12 to 25 can apply for the Top Influencers feature.
first_step.basis: Volunteer and application routes are listed, though the steps are not spelled out.

records.notes: No dates are listed on the home page, so status is probably_active. Volunteer coach or mentor roles are not described. Program listings may change, so check the site before sending anyone.
